anchors.note: The authors also take the similarity to suggest a different mechanism from Parkinson's disease; no people with Parkinson's disease were studied. In percentage terms the caudate reduction (27.8%) was somewhat larger than the putamen reduction (21.1%).

for_senior_author: Interpretation gap (reader 2 agrees: substantial): consider adding that the discussion raises a later-life parkinsonism risk from methamphetamine-related plus age-related DAT decline (p. 380), which the data do not test.

Risk of bias (reader 2 agrees: high overall): reader 2 notes that selection of the reported result is a concern for the cognitive outcomes much more than for the DAT outcome; decide whether to rate the two outcomes separately.
not_added: Key finding 6: reader 2 notes the same point is also made in the preceding paragraph (p. 381); confirmed, the cited summary paragraph is correct as it stands.
